introduction: These short passages say that a religious community attracts by its affection before its arguments: the unity of the friends “is very important”, strangers are to be treated as kin, a member who feels neglected should be sought out, and “a spirit of prejudice-free, loving comradeship” does more than “any amount of words”. The first Christian community is described in the same terms in Acts, “of one heart and of one soul”, and in Tertullian’s report of what outsiders said; John’s letters make love of the brother the test of love of God. Jesus’s “if ye salute your brethren only” and Burke’s “little platoon” raise the question every warm community faces, whether its love stops at its own door.
questions: Reading 2 concerns one person who felt the friends had cooled. What does a community owe the member who drifts?
“See how they love one another.” What would an outsider see in the communities you know?
How does a close community keep its warmth from becoming exclusiveness?

outside.why: Be loving to all peoples with heart and soul. A certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him.
Friends grew cool, thinking she no longer had time for them. Let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together.
News of unity and love among the friends. The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.
See the stranger as kin. The stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself.
A Bahá’í by deed. Let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
Associate with all the earth’s peoples in kindliness. If ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others?
The unity of the friends is the important thing. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
What pagans said of the early Christians, according to Tertullian: see how they love one another; how they are ready even to die for one another.
The love of man is essential to the love of God. He that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?

Believers must come to feel they are one spiritual family. Burke: to love the little platoon we belong to in society is the first link in the series by which we proceed towards a love to our country and to mankind. Can love of one’s own community lead outward, as he says, or does it turn inward?
Without real love the Cause cannot bring in numbers. Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass.
Loving comradeship opens eyes more than words. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.

The atmosphere of the community is what holds new believers. They continued daily with one accord, breaking bread from house to house, with gladness and singleness of heart; and the Lord added to the church daily.
